item.title: China: English to be removed as a graded core subject?
item.description: A university professor is calling for English to no longer be taught as a graded core subject in Chinese schools. Opponents argue that, in a globalized world, knowing English is beneficial for the country and career.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany's connection to the September 11, 2001 attacks
item.description: The 9/11 attacks were partly planned in Hamburg, via the so-called Hamburg cell, whose members played key roles in the plot. A look back at a day that shook up Germany’s approach to national security.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
item.description: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran tightens social control with crackdown on cafes
item.description: Authorities are keeping a close eye on cafes, fearing they could play a role in fostering anti-government sentiment.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ethiopia's constitutional reform: What does it mean — especially for Abiy?
item.description: Does Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed stand to benefit from a planned constitutional reform in the country? A new presidential system would reshape political power — and could give him even more power in office.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Syria arms depot explosion kills at least 14
item.description: The explosion struck near the Syrian city of Sarmada in Idlib province in the northwest. The Defense Ministry said the weapons and remnants from the war were being stored temporarily at the site before being relocated.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Cambodia's floating schools hit by rising fuel costs
item.description: The Iran war has sent fuel prices higher in Cambodia, squeezing families who rely on fishing and boats for their livelihoods. For children living on Tonle Sap, rising fuel costs pose yet another barrier to education.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Syria: How the 'house of sisters' threat split society
item.description: Rumor has it that the 'house of sisters' is where kidnapped women from other Syrian sects are forced to convert to Islam. Nobody knows if it really exists, but it's being used to create communal tensions anyway.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trafficked into fraud: An African crisis situation in Cambodia
item.description: Cambodia's crackdown on scam operators is stranding young African trafficking victims in the Asian country with no money, no passport and no prospects.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
item.description: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trump takes center stage at Republican midterm convention
item.description: With Trump's approval rating at 33%, some Republican candidates are keeping their distance. Could putting him at the heart of the 2026 midterms backfire?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
item.description: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.

item.title: How Mao Zedong's legacy still shapes China 50 years on
item.description: China has transformed since Mao Zedong's death 50 years ago. But his legacy endures — from Xi Jinping's rule to a new wave of Mao nostalgia among young Chinese.
